issue_context.title: [networkd] Support for complete set of CAN interface options
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The SocketCAN brings multiple options which might be set. Most of drivers support only subset of them, yet option list is a bit longer than currently supported by networkd.
The `>` markers indicate options which are supported by networkd while `-` indicate an missing option or options:

```
Usage: ip link set DEVICE type can
>	[ bitrate BITRATE [ sample-point SAMPLE-POINT] ] |
-	[ tq TQ prop-seg PROP_SEG phase-seg1 PHASE-SEG1
- 	  phase-seg2 PHASE-SEG2 [ sjw SJW ] ]

>	[ dbitrate BITRATE [ dsample-point SAMPLE-POINT] ] |
-	[ dtq TQ dprop-seg PROP_SEG dphase-seg1 PHASE-SEG1
- 	  dphase-seg2 PHASE-SEG2 [ dsjw SJW ] ]

-	[ loopback { on | off } ]
>	[ listen-only { on | off } ]
>	[ triple-sampling { on | off } ]
-	[ one-shot { on | off } ]
>	[ berr-reporting { on | off } ]
>	[ fd { on | off } ]
>	[ fd-non-iso { on | off } ]
-	[ presume-ack { on | off } ]
-	[ cc-len8-dlc { on | off } ]

>	[ restart-ms TIME-MS ]
	[ restart ]

?	[ termination { 0..65535 } ]

	Where: BITRATE	:= { 1..1000000 }
		  SAMPLE-POINT	:= { 0.000..0.999 }
		  TQ		:= { NUMBER }
		  PROP-SEG	:= { 1..8 }
		  PHASE-SEG1	:= { 1..8 }
		  PHASE-SEG2	:= { 1..8 }
		  SJW		:= { 1..4 }
		  RESTART-MS	:= { 0 | NUMBER }
```


There is a `Termination` option available in networkd CAN settings which is still not documented within kernel docs. This option is however a number and not switch, please see https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/12a6075cabc0d9ffbc0366b44daa22f278606312. From commit you can see that termination option allows to pick a resistor of certain kind. Obviously, for most of the cases it will be 120. Since `networkd` does not know actual device (end user shall do) staying with a boolean switch will make it impossible to use termination option.
The low level options may be considered rather optional, yet loopback is something quite useful for testing usecases.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Consistent support for socketcan interface options.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is to fallback to unit files and scripts which do the same. Yet then whole point of use of managed network configuration is gone.

**The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for**
`systemd 248`

review_comments: so, the value "0" is parsed as boolean here, not as termination ohm value. This is intended? There's no ambiguity here?
Ouch. Nice catch. "0" has fortunately no ambiguity, but "1" must be handled as 1 ohm instead of true.
